parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized ESM .mjs output, local-only imports, manual argv parsing, base58 encode/decode parity, Python bytes repr formatting, BigInt precision, and no Buffer or Uint8Array use.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first probed reference behavior, then assigned distinct ownership: codec files to agent-0, parser to agent-1, pyformat and entry point to agent-2, with the parent retaining integration and verification.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote the initial modules under /output/lib and /output/test14.mjs. After integrated tests, the parent replaced the negative guard in base58.mjs with Python-style floor division and simplified the entry catch path.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent consumed the aggregate swarm result, ran the combined entry point, edited the integrated files, listed the final /output tree, and delivered test14.mjs plus four library modules.
parallel.verification: The run checked reference samples, parser errors, codec unit cases, pyformat cases, assembled sample and edge outputs, negative-input hang parity via timeout, and a forbidden construct scan.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No visible unfinished parallel deliverable remained at closure; official evaluation passed all 131 cases.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same ESM, .mjs, CLI, no-dependency, BigInt, and output-format requirements and probed the executable for sample, zero, missing-argument, big-int, and negative-input behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main agent owned all modules: alphabet, encode, decode, parser, and entry point, with no delegation or subagent activity.
serial.implementation: The serial implementation wrote a separate base58 directory and CLI parser, encoded non-negative BigInts, returned Number only for safe decoded values, printed decodedInt directly, and threw for negative encode.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial entry point wired its modules together and produced the expected artifact tree, but no later patch reconciled the observed negative-input hang or unsafe BigInt decode formatting risk.
serial.verification: The serial run verified the four sample cases, zero, one large positive encode case, missing required argument behavior, and observed a reference negative-input hang.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial final response explicitly left negative input as a thrown error instead of the reference hang, and official evaluation failed 6 of 131 cases.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the core contract and sample behavior but left at least one reference-behavior divergence in the final solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split codec, parser, and formatting/entry files across three subagents while the parent owned integration and final fixes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one actor write all modules and retain all decisions locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used distinct component owners plus a parent integrator; serial used a single implementation owner and no handoffs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a detailed pinned interface contract for local modules, then the parent revised a behavior contract after further black-box evidence.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial made all interface decisions internally and did not need cross-agent contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more explicit component boundaries, but the key edge correction came from parent follow-up rather than from a child handoff.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ended with a floor-division base58 encoder, BigInt decode, bytesRepr, formatInt, and a final entry point that formats decoded integers explicitly.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a negative guard and direct decodedInt logging after returning BigInt for unsafe decoded values.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel patched the edge behavior and output formatting path; serial left the known negative case as an exception and had a decode formatting path that could diverge from Python.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All three subagent results returned to the parent, which inspected the aggregate output, joined the implementation, and then took over final correction.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and all results stayed in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's child work was retrieved and used rather than lost; the remaining difference was the parent's post-handoff correction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a coherent final /output tree under a parent-managed file layout after the children used assigned file scopes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a coherent artifact tree in a different directory layout but with the entry and module files present.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no evidence that shared-state collision explains the outcome; the material difference is in behavior inside the delivered code.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed assembled sample and edge verification after patching, including a timeout check showing negative-input hang parity and a clean forbidden-construct scan.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified sample and some edge behavior but ended after acknowledging its negative-input behavior differed from the reference.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's verification loop changed the implementation before closure; serial's verification surfaced a mismatch but did not convert it into a fix.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used more wall-clock and LLM budget, but finished with all subagents complete, post-integration verification, and a passing official result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial closed faster with no delegation, but the shorter path left a known edge divergence and failed official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Budget pressure did not cause parallel failure; the serial run's faster closure skipped a behavior correction that parallel spent time making.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current status records show parallel passed 131/131 and serial failed 125/131. The trajectory difference is concrete: parallel's parent detected that the reference executable timed out on negative input, replaced the child-produced negative guard with Python-style floor-division behavior, and verified assembled sample, edge, and hang-parity behavior. Serial produced a sample-passing implementation but its own negative-input run threw an exception while the reference stayed running, and it finalized while explicitly saying it did not mirror that behavior. Serial also had a decoded integer path that returned BigInt for unsafe decoded values and printed it directly, while parallel formatted decoded BigInts through formatInt. The exact hidden failures are not listed in the mounted evaluation summary, so these are supported comparative contributors rather than an exclusive root-cause claim.
parallel_contributors: Parent corrected the base58 encoder after observing reference negative-input timeout behavior.
Parent reran integrated sample, edge, hang-parity, and forbidden-construct checks before closing.
serial_contributors: Serial left negative encode as a thrown error despite observing the reference executable hang.
Serial printed decodedInt directly after returning BigInt for unsafe decoded values, unlike Python decimal int formatting.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial's negative-input behavior diverged from the reference executable.
Serial's unsafe decoded BigInt formatting path could emit a Node BigInt suffix instead of Python decimal text.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: No active child was stopped before needed work finalized; all three subagents completed and returned results.
The parent finalized the usable candidate after verification; no complete candidate sat unpromoted until closure.
The relevant patch to base58.mjs occurred before the final integrated verification sweep, not after it.
Delegated implementation was retrievable and joined; the parent used the child modules as the basis for the final tree.
There was no verifier child whose concrete finding was trapped below the parent; verification was parent-run after integration.
No child failed or was cancelled; when the codec behavior needed correction, the parent took over and patched it.
The completed child results were inspected and incorporated; the parent proceeded consistently with the handoffs after patching.
The parent used timeout observations to change implementation behavior rather than waiting blindly until closure.
Parallel children were assigned different files and did not produce competing designs for the same behavior needing reconciliation.
No two live agents edited the same file and had to reconcile a concurrent same-file change.
The parent later edited child-created source after handoff, but this was sequential takeover, not a live overwrite of another active owner's source.
The entry point was edited only as part of parent-controlled final correction, not overwritten while another live agent owned or used it.

Although children wrote under shared /output, assigned file scopes avoided unstable state or provenance ambiguity.
No generated cache, fixture, temporary path, or auxiliary artifact from one actor was consumed as a reference by another actor.
